hero.title: EXPLORE THE COSMOS AND DISCOVER NEW WORLDS THROUGH TIME
hero.subtitle: Analyze more than a billion objects captured by NASA's SPHEREx mission. Compare epochs, filter 102 infrared bands and help us find asteroids, brown dwarfs and the next great astronomical discovery with EON.

hook.title: Did you know that comparing two photos of the sky led to the discovery of Pluto?
hook.text: The universe is not static. Every six months, the SPHEREx mission maps the entire sky. By comparing images from different dates, points of light that change position reveal comets, asteroids and hidden bodies that no algorithm can analyze on its own. You could be the one who finds the next one.

compare.caption: Illustrative demo: the stars stay fixed; the marked object changes position between the two captures.

spherex.title: What is the SPHEREx mission?
spherex.text: Launched in <hl>2025</hl>, SPHEREx is NASA's space observatory that scans the entire sky <hl>every six months</hl>. Unlike conventional telescopes, it observes the cosmos in <hl>102 bands</hl> of near-infrared light, making it possible to detect the chemical fingerprint of essential molecules such as water, carbon and hydrogen in more than a billion objects (from distant galaxies and quasars to nearby comets).

planetX.title: In search of Planet X and hidden worlds
planetX.text: At the edges of our solar system and beyond, there are celestial bodies too cold and dark to be seen with the naked eye: from brown dwarfs (massive bodies halfway between a giant planet and a star) to the hypothetical Planet X. Although they barely emit visible light, they shine in SPHEREx's infrared spectrum and give themselves away by slowly moving from one time capture to the next. With Aetheris, anyone can track these moving anomalies.
planetX.imageAlt: Star field with a faint object glowing in infrared

features.title: Much more than a gallery
features.subtitle: Discover different ways to explore the universe with Aetheris.

timelapse.label: Time view
timelapse.title: 1. Time Evolution (Timelapse)
timelapse.description: View sequences of images captured every 6 months as a video, or subtract captures from different dates. Instantly identify asteroids, comets and nearby objects by how they move across the sky.

search.label: Search view (Coordinates)
search.title: 2. Coordinate Exploration
search.description: Navigate to any region of the cosmos by entering its Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec). Adjust the field of view to track fast-moving sources and share findings through direct links.

spectral.label: Spectrum view
spectral.title: 3. Infrared Spectral Analysis
spectral.description: Explore SPHEREx's 102 infrared light bands and its 6 detector arrays. Filter wavelengths to tell apart the chemical composition of stars, brown dwarfs and galaxies.

astronomy.title: Astronomy

exploration.title: Exploration

hero.text: Explore the satellite's control panel. Each screen is a module of the observatory: scroll down and discover them step by step.

timelapse.label: Timelapse
timelapse.title: The sky through time
timelapse.text: It joins images of the same patch of sky taken on different dates and plays them like a video: whatever moves or changes brightness could be an asteroid, a comet or a variable star.
timelapse.filmStripAria: Five frames in which an object moves
timelapse.hint: You can also click the satellite's screen.

search.label: Search
search.title: Find a point of interest
search.text: Every point in the sky has an "address", just like latitude and longitude on Earth. Type it in and the camera travels to that region.
search.decHelp: Like latitude: from −90° to +90° from the celestial equator.
search.hint: You can also click the satellite's screen.

spectral.label: Spectral Explorer
spectral.title: The 102 channels of SPHEREx
spectral.text: SPHEREx doesn't take a single photo: it splits infrared light into {{channels}} channels, from {{min}} µm to {{max}} µm. Each channel reveals something different, such as water ice, dust or distant galaxies.
spectral.hint: Move the control (the knobs respond) or click the satellite's screen.

timelapse.title: The sky through time
timelapse.text: Choose a region and a date range to watch its images like a video. Click on an object that changes to analyze it.
timelapse.noObsText: Try a wider date range, another band or a larger field of view.
timelapse.chooseText: Enter RA, Dec, field of view and dates, then press “Search region”.

search.title: Find a point of <hl>interest</hl>
search.text: Compare a region's observations with image or blink, and click on an object to analyze it.

actions.title: Actions
actions.singleHelp: Shows the observation from epoch A.
actions.blinkUnavailable: Blink requires two distinct real acquisition epochs.
actions.blinkHelp: Alternates two aligned real epochs. Visual differences do not establish motion or variability.

spectral.title: See one point across SPHEREx's <hl>102 channels</hl>
spectral.text: The image shows one of the 102 layers in the DR1 HiPS cube. Change channels to see another wavelength; click the image to plot that point's intensity across all 102 channels.
spectral.firstDownload: The first request for a region downloads its official FITS tile (~321 MB). Later requests reuse the stored product.
spectral.clickHint: Click a point to plot its spectrum
spectral.searchHint: Enter RA, Dec and field of view, then press GO.
spectral.cubeText: 102 layers of the same region; the viewer shows one at a time. The colors in this diagram are not physical colors.
spectral.objectsEmpty: There is no curve yet. Click the image to sample one pixel across 102 channels and compare up to {{max}} points. This is an exploratory view, not object photometry.
spectral.qualityTitle: NHITS: contributing pixels; FLAGS: raw bit mask without interpretation
